exclusion_detail: Lead compound 7 (N-benzyl-4-(1,2,4-triazol-4-yl)aniline) is 'an accidental product' separated during the preparation of 5b; it has no procedure of its own (only a yield and spectra), the benzylating agent for 5b/7 is never named (general procedure uses R'X), and the paper does not say how the acetyl group is lost. Net 4a + benzyl halide -> 7 is the only reading, but it would be a guess for the reagent and mechanism.

lead.why: Abstract: 'Especially compound 7 exhibited higher levels of efficacy than the reference standard fluoxetine in the FST and the tail suspension test' (also the featured compound in the open field test and the conclusions).

reactions.conditions: Ac2O (2 equiv), AcOH, 120 C, 6 h; poured into water; 86.8%.
HC(OEt)3 (3 equiv), formylhydrazine (3 equiv), isopropanol (text) / EtOH (scheme), 90 C, 12 h; 78% (75% in characterisation).

General alkylation: CH3ONa (2 equiv), TEBA (0.1 equiv), CH3CN, 60 C (text) / 80 C (scheme), 18 h. 7 was separated as a by-product alongside 5b (N-acetyl-N-benzyl, 26%); 7 isolated in 45%. Benzyl halide identity is an assumption (bromide by analogy with 1-bromopentane for 5a).

notes: Main text only (no SI file; the text layer has the full experimental). Transcription is supplied although the paper is excluded, so a reviewer can overrule: it is a literal reading in which 7 comes from 4a in the benzylation step. Internal inconsistencies: solvent for step 3 (isopropanol in text, EtOH in scheme), temperature for alkylation (60 vs 80 C), 3a/4a yield numbers. other_qualifying: 4a is 3 steps; 5a (pentyl bromide) and 6a/6e (via 2b/3b/4b with propionic anhydride then alkyl halide) are 4 steps; 6e uses an unnamed benzyl halide too, so strictly only 4a, 4b and 5a (named 1-bromopentane) and 6a (propyl halide unnamed) are fully explicit; list is optimistic for 6a and 6e.
